geometry_edits.rationale: Align the public threshold cut to the verified frontage/access edge so the entry seam reads directly on the access side.
Deepen the access cut slightly so the ground response becomes more legible without weakening the dominant hall mass.
Keep the notch proportioned as a clear entry/service articulation rather than a large void that would compete with the main hall.
Shift the roof/section language toward a folded profile to strengthen span and daylight expression while preserving the continuous hall gesture.
Maintain the long-span reading along the existing elongated axis.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent low horizontal hall mass with a clear dominant body and a subordinate notch/cut on one side, which aligns well with the gymnasium brief. Across the four views the form stays legible, the silhouette is continuous, and there is no obvious view-to-view collision or fragmentation. The main weakness is that the public response to the verified access edge is modest: the notch is present, but the ground/entry void is not especially pronounced or welcoming. The roof/section language is acceptable for a compact training hall, though it is somewhat generic compared with the stronger daylight/section character in some references. Overall, this is program-fit and repairable, not rejected.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Single dominant low-rise hall with an articulated roof plane and a subordinate edge condition; good precedent for keeping one clear mass while adding a legible public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Mixed-use support campus rather than a single hall; spatial dispersion is only partially transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Dispersed low pavilions and terraced/courtyard relations can inform a public ground sequence, but the candidate should not fragment into separate objects.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More sculptural and irregular than the current candidate; do not copy the faceting language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A monolithic low-rise body with selective cutouts and roof articulation suggests how to keep a strong primary mass while opening a controlled entry side.
Long horizontal pavilion logic with open perimeter/courtyard relations supports the idea of a public forecourt or carved edge to the access side.
Clear hall volume plus a strong roof section profile; useful for preserving a dominant enclosed volume while improving roof legibility.

warnings: The access-edge response could be more legible as a public void or entry seam.
The section is coherent but somewhat understated for a gymnasium if stronger daylight/roof expression is desired.
